title: Sinigang na bangus
intro: Milkfish steaks simmered in fresh tamarind broth with radish, eggplant, okra and water spinach. A light, everyday fish sinigang with a clean, sharp sourness.

items.name: large milkfish (bangus)
items.note: about 800 g, scaled, cleaned and cut into 5 or 6 pieces

items.name: bunch water spinach (kangkong)
items.note: leaves and tender stems, about 200 g

steps.text: Bring the water, onion and tomatoes to a boil, then simmer until the tomatoes soften.
Meanwhile, boil the tamarind in the 2 cups of water until the skins split and the flesh turns soft.
Mash the tamarind in its water with a fork, then press it through a strainer into a bowl. Discard the seeds and skins and keep the thick sour juice.
Add the radish and simmer until it starts to turn translucent.
Add the fish, lower the heat and simmer gently without stirring until the fish is just cooked.
Add the eggplant and okra and simmer until tender.
Stir in the tamarind juice to taste, add the chilies and season with fish sauce.
Turn off the heat, add the water spinach and cover until wilted. Serve hot.

tips: Shake the pot instead of stirring once the fish is in, so the pieces stay whole.

title: Sinigang na bangus sa bayabas
intro: Milkfish in a fragrant broth soured with ripe guavas, which pair especially well with the rich fish. Mild, fruity sourness and a sweet aroma.

items.name: large milkfish (bangus)
items.note: about 800 g, scaled, cleaned and cut into 5 or 6 pieces

items.name: bunch water spinach (kangkong)
items.note: leaves and tender stems, about 200 g

steps.text: Bring the water, onion, tomatoes and guavas to a boil, then simmer until the guavas are very soft.
Scoop out the guavas and mash them through a strainer back into the pot. Discard the seeds and skins.
Add the fish, lower the heat and simmer gently without stirring until just cooked.
Add the eggplant and long beans and simmer until tender.
Add the chilies and season with fish sauce.
Turn off the heat, add the water spinach and cover until wilted. Serve hot.

tips: Some cooks leave a few guava halves in the pot for serving. They are soft and good to eat with the broth.

title: Sinigang na bangus sa miso
intro: Milkfish in a cloudy, savory broth made with sauteed miso, tomatoes and ginger, soured with tamarind and finished with mustard greens. Earthy, salty and sour all at once.

items.name: large milkfish (bangus)
items.note: about 800 g, scaled, cleaned and cut into 5 or 6 pieces

steps.text: First, boil the tamarind in the 2 cups of water until the skins split and the flesh turns soft.
Mash the tamarind in its water with a fork, then press it through a strainer into a bowl. Discard the seeds and skins and keep the thick sour juice.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Saute the garlic, onion and ginger until fragrant, then the tomatoes until they break down.
Add the miso and stir for a minute until it smells toasty.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil and simmer so the miso flavors the broth.
Add the radish and simmer until it starts to turn translucent.
Add the fish and simmer gently without stirring until just cooked.
Add the eggplant and long beans and simmer until tender.
Stir in the tamarind juice to taste, add the chilies and season with fish sauce.
Add the mustard greens and simmer briefly until they wilt. Serve hot.

tips: Miso brands vary in saltiness. Add the fish sauce only at the end, after tasting.

title: Sinigang na bangus belly
intro: Boneless milkfish belly cooked in tamarind broth, rich and silky with no bones to pick through. The fat from the belly makes the sour broth taste fuller.

items.name: bunch water spinach (kangkong)
items.note: leaves and tender stems, about 200 g

steps.text: Bring the water, onion and tomatoes to a boil, then simmer until the tomatoes soften.
Meanwhile, boil the tamarind in the 2 cups of water until the skins split and the flesh turns soft.
Mash the tamarind in its water with a fork, then press it through a strainer into a bowl. Discard the seeds and skins and keep the thick sour juice.
Add the radish and simmer until it starts to turn translucent.
Add the okra and simmer until almost tender.
Stir in the tamarind juice to taste, add the chilies and season with fish sauce.
Slide in the fish belly and simmer gently until just opaque. Belly cooks fast and breaks apart if overcooked.
Turn off the heat, add the water spinach and cover until wilted. Serve right away.

tips: Frozen bangus belly works well. Thaw it in the fridge and pat it dry so it does not cloud the broth.

title: Sinigang na bangus sa kamias
intro: Milkfish simmered with fresh kamias and a little ginger until the broth turns bright and puckery. Simple, tart and clean-tasting.

items.name: large milkfish (bangus)
items.note: about 800 g, scaled, cleaned and cut into 5 or 6 pieces

steps.text: Bring the water, onion, tomatoes and ginger to a boil, then simmer until the tomatoes soften.
Add the kamias and simmer until soft and olive green. Press some against the side of the pot.
Add the fish, lower the heat and simmer gently without stirring until just cooked.
Add the eggplant and okra and simmer until tender.
Add the chilies and season with fish sauce.
Turn off the heat, add the bok choy and cover until it wilts. Serve hot.

tips: Kamias that are slightly yellow are less sour. Use more of them, or mix in a few green ones.

title: Sinigang na ulo ng salmon sa miso
intro: Salmon head simmered in a miso and tamarind broth with mustard greens, radish and eggplant. The rich, fatty fish and salty miso make a deeply savory sour soup.

items.name: salmon heads
items.note: split and cut into large pieces, gills removed

steps.text: First, boil the tamarind in the 2 cups of water until the skins split and the flesh turns soft.
Mash the tamarind in its water with a fork, then press it through a strainer into a bowl. Discard the seeds and skins and keep the thick sour juice.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Saute the garlic, onion and ginger until fragrant, then the tomatoes until they break down.
Add the miso and stir for a minute until it smells toasty.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil and add the radish. Simmer until it starts to turn translucent.
Add the salmon heads and simmer gently until the flesh is cooked through.
Add the eggplant and long beans and simmer until tender.
Stir in the tamarind juice to taste, add the chilies and season with fish sauce.
Add the mustard greens and simmer briefly until they wilt. Serve hot.

tips: Ask the fish counter to split the heads and remove the gills: gills make the broth bitter.

title: Sinigang na salmon belly
intro: Strips of salmon belly cooked briefly in a sharp tamarind broth with radish, okra and bok choy. Rich and buttery fish against a very sour soup.

steps.text: Bring the water, onion and tomatoes to a boil, then simmer until the tomatoes soften.
Meanwhile, boil the tamarind in the 2 cups of water until the skins split and the flesh turns soft.
Mash the tamarind in its water with a fork, then press it through a strainer into a bowl. Discard the seeds and skins and keep the thick sour juice.
Add the radish and simmer until it starts to turn translucent.
Add the okra and simmer until almost tender.
Stir in the tamarind juice to taste, add the chilies and season with fish sauce.
Add the salmon belly and simmer gently until just cooked.
Turn off the heat, add the bok choy and cover until it wilts. Serve right away.

tips: Salmon belly releases a lot of fat. Skim some off the top before serving if you like a lighter broth.

title: Sinigang na tilapia
intro: Whole tilapia simmered in tamarind broth with a few slices of ginger, radish, long beans and water spinach. An affordable, everyday fish sinigang.

items.name: medium tilapia
items.note: about 1 kg total, scaled, gutted and halved crosswise

items.name: bunch water spinach (kangkong)
items.note: leaves and tender stems, about 200 g

steps.text: Bring the water, onion, tomatoes and ginger to a boil, then simmer until the tomatoes soften.
Meanwhile, boil the tamarind in the 2 cups of water until the skins split and the flesh turns soft.
Mash the tamarind in its water with a fork, then press it through a strainer into a bowl. Discard the seeds and skins and keep the thick sour juice.
Add the radish and simmer until it starts to turn translucent.
Add the tilapia, lower the heat and simmer gently without stirring until the flesh flakes.
Add the long beans and simmer until tender.
Stir in the tamarind juice to taste, add the chilies and season with fish sauce.
Turn off the heat, add the water spinach and cover until wilted. Serve hot.

tips: Ginger helps tame the muddy taste some farmed tilapia has. Scrape the dark lining inside the belly cavity for the same reason.

title: Sinigang na tilapia sa miso
intro: Tilapia in a broth of sauteed miso, tomatoes and onion, soured with tamarind and finished with mustard greens. Savory, earthy and sour.

items.name: medium tilapia
items.note: about 1 kg total, scaled, gutted and halved crosswise

steps.text: First, boil the tamarind in the 2 cups of water until the skins split and the flesh turns soft.
Mash the tamarind in its water with a fork, then press it through a strainer into a bowl. Discard the seeds and skins and keep the thick sour juice.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Saute the garlic and onion until soft, then the tomatoes until they break down.
Add the miso and stir for a minute until it smells toasty.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil and simmer so the miso flavors the broth.
Add the tilapia, lower the heat and simmer gently without stirring until the flesh flakes.
Add the okra and long beans and simmer until tender.
Stir in the tamarind juice to taste, add the chilies and season with fish sauce.
Add the mustard greens and simmer briefly until they wilt. Serve hot.

tips: Mustard greens can be quite bitter. Blanch them in the broth for only a minute or two to keep them bright and mild.

title: Sinigang na maya-maya
intro: Red snapper steaks and head simmered in tamarind broth, sweet and firm-fleshed against the sharp sourness. A sinigang for when the market has good fresh snapper.

items.name: red snapper (maya-maya)
items.note: scaled, cleaned and cut into steaks, head split and gills removed

items.name: bunch water spinach (kangkong)
items.note: leaves and tender stems, about 200 g

steps.text: Bring the water, onion and tomatoes to a boil, then simmer until the tomatoes soften.
Meanwhile, boil the tamarind in the 2 cups of water until the skins split and the flesh turns soft.
Mash the tamarind in its water with a fork, then press it through a strainer into a bowl. Discard the seeds and skins and keep the thick sour juice.
Add the radish and simmer until it starts to turn translucent.
Add the fish head first, then the steaks a few minutes later. Simmer gently without stirring until cooked through.
Add the okra and long beans and simmer until tender.
Stir in the tamarind juice to taste, add the chilies and season with fish sauce.
Turn off the heat, add the water spinach and cover until wilted. Serve hot.

tips: The head gives the broth most of its flavor, so do not skip it. The cheeks are the best bite in the pot.

title: Sinigang na lapu-lapu sa miso
intro: Grouper steaks in a miso and tamarind broth with eggplant, radish and mustard greens. The firm, sweet fish holds up well in the savory, sour soup.

items.name: grouper (lapu-lapu)
items.note: scaled, cleaned and cut into steaks

steps.text: First, boil the tamarind in the 2 cups of water until the skins split and the flesh turns soft.
Mash the tamarind in its water with a fork, then press it through a strainer into a bowl. Discard the seeds and skins and keep the thick sour juice.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Saute the garlic, onion and ginger until fragrant, then the tomatoes until they break down.
Add the miso and stir for a minute until it smells toasty.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil and add the radish. Simmer until it starts to turn translucent.
Add the fish and simmer gently without stirring until cooked through.
Add the eggplant and simmer until tender.
Stir in the tamarind juice to taste, add the chilies and season with fish sauce.
Add the mustard greens and simmer briefly until they wilt. Serve hot.

tips: Lapu-lapu has thick skin that holds the steaks together. Leave it on.

title: Sinigang na tanigue
intro: Thick Spanish mackerel steaks simmered in tamarind broth with ginger, eggplant, okra and bok choy. Meaty fish and a bright, sour soup.

steps.text: Bring the water, onion, tomatoes and ginger to a boil, then simmer until the tomatoes soften.
Meanwhile, boil the tamarind in the 2 cups of water until the skins split and the flesh turns soft.
Mash the tamarind in its water with a fork, then press it through a strainer into a bowl. Discard the seeds and skins and keep the thick sour juice.
Add the radish and simmer until it starts to turn translucent.
Add the fish steaks and simmer gently without stirring until just cooked.
Add the eggplant and okra and simmer until tender.
Stir in the tamarind juice to taste, add the chilies and season with fish sauce.
Turn off the heat, add the bok choy and cover until it wilts. Serve hot.

tips: Tanigue dries out if it boils hard. Keep the broth at a gentle simmer once the fish is in.

title: Sinigang na pusit
intro: Tender squid rings cooked for just a minute or two in a sharp tamarind broth with radish, okra and long beans. Sweet, clean and very sour.

items.name: medium squid
items.note: cleaned, ink sacs and quills removed, body cut into rings

items.name: bunch water spinach (kangkong)
items.note: leaves and tender stems, about 200 g

steps.text: Bring the water, onion and tomatoes to a boil, then simmer until the tomatoes soften.
Meanwhile, boil the tamarind in the 2 cups of water until the skins split and the flesh turns soft.
Mash the tamarind in its water with a fork, then press it through a strainer into a bowl. Discard the seeds and skins and keep the thick sour juice.
Add the radish and simmer until it starts to turn translucent.
Add the okra and long beans and simmer until tender.
Stir in the tamarind juice to taste, add the chilies and season with fish sauce.
Add the squid and simmer just until it turns opaque.
Turn off the heat, add the water spinach and cover until wilted. Serve right away.

tips: Squid turns rubbery past 2 or 3 minutes. Add it last and serve as soon as the greens wilt.

title: Sinigang na alimango
intro: Mud crabs simmered in tamarind broth with ginger, radish and okra, so the sweet crab juices mix into the sour soup. A special-occasion sinigang eaten with your hands.

items.name: live mud crabs (alimango)
items.note: 2 or 3 crabs, scrubbed, halved and cleaned

items.name: bunch water spinach (kangkong)
items.note: leaves and tender stems, about 200 g

steps.text: Chill the crabs in the freezer until sluggish, then scrub them, pull off the top shell, remove the gills and halve the bodies. Crack the claws lightly with the back of a knife.
Bring the water, onion, tomatoes and ginger to a boil, then simmer until the tomatoes soften.
Meanwhile, boil the tamarind in the 2 cups of water until the skins split and the flesh turns soft.
Mash the tamarind in its water with a fork, then press it through a strainer into a bowl. Discard the seeds and skins and keep the thick sour juice.
Add the radish and simmer until it starts to turn translucent.
Add the crabs, cover and simmer until the shells turn bright orange-red.
Add the okra and long beans and simmer until tender.
Stir in the tamarind juice to taste, add the chilies and season with fish sauce.
Turn off the heat, add the water spinach and cover until wilted. Serve hot.

tips: Keep the orange crab fat in the top shells and add them to the pot with the crabs. It enriches the broth.

title: Sinigang na panga ng tuna
intro: Tuna jaw simmered in tamarind broth with ginger and vegetables until the rich, fatty meat around the bone turns tender. Hearty and very savory for a fish sinigang.

items.name: bunch water spinach (kangkong)
items.note: leaves and tender stems, about 200 g

steps.text: Bring the water, onion, tomatoes and ginger to a boil, then simmer until the tomatoes soften.
Add the tuna jaw, skim off any foam, and simmer gently until the meat comes away from the bone.
Meanwhile, boil the tamarind in the 2 cups of water until the skins split and the flesh turns soft.
Mash the tamarind in its water with a fork, then press it through a strainer into a bowl. Discard the seeds and skins and keep the thick sour juice.
Add the radish and simmer until it starts to turn translucent.
Add the eggplant and okra and simmer until tender.
Stir in the tamarind juice to taste, add the chilies and season with fish sauce.
Turn off the heat, add the water spinach and cover until wilted. Serve hot.

tips: Rinse the jaw well and trim off any dark, bloody bits before cooking for a cleaner-tasting broth.

title: Sinigang na dalag
intro: Mudfish slices simmered in tamarind broth with radish, long beans and plenty of water spinach. The firm, sweet freshwater fish stays whole in the sour soup.

items.name: bunch water spinach (kangkong)
items.note: leaves and tender stems, about 200 g

steps.text: Rub the fish slices all over with the coarse salt to remove the slime, then rinse well.
Bring the water, onion and tomatoes to a boil, then simmer until the tomatoes soften.
Meanwhile, boil the tamarind in the 2 cups of water until the skins split and the flesh turns soft.
Mash the tamarind in its water with a fork, then press it through a strainer into a bowl. Discard the seeds and skins and keep the thick sour juice.
Add the radish and simmer until it starts to turn translucent.
Add the fish and simmer gently without stirring until cooked through.
Add the long beans and simmer until tender.
Stir in the tamarind juice to taste, add the chilies and season with fish sauce.
Turn off the heat, add the water spinach and cover until wilted. Serve hot.

tips: Ask the fish vendor to kill and clean the dalag for you. Scrubbing well with salt is what keeps the broth from tasting muddy.

title: Sinigang na galunggong sa kamias
intro: Whole round scad simmered with fresh kamias, ginger and tomatoes. An everyday budget sinigang with a tart, clean broth.

items.name: bunch water spinach (kangkong)
items.note: leaves and tender stems, about 200 g

steps.text: Bring the water, onion, tomatoes and ginger to a boil, then simmer until the tomatoes soften.
Add the kamias and simmer until soft and olive green. Press some against the side of the pot.
Lay the fish in the pot and simmer gently without stirring until cooked through.
Add the eggplant and long beans and simmer until tender.
Add the chilies and season with fish sauce.
Turn off the heat, add the water spinach and cover until wilted. Serve hot.

tips: Pick galunggong with bright, clear eyes and firm bodies. Tilt the pot to baste them instead of stirring so they do not break.

title: Seafood sinigang
intro: Fish, mussels, shrimp and squid in one pot of tamarind broth with radish, okra and long beans. Each seafood goes in at its own time, so everything stays tender.

items.name: firm white fish fillet or steaks
items.note: such as maya-maya or lapu-lapu, cut into large pieces

items.name: bunch water spinach (kangkong)
items.note: leaves and tender stems, about 200 g

steps.text: Bring the water, onion, tomatoes and ginger to a boil, then simmer until the tomatoes soften.
Meanwhile, boil the tamarind in the 2 cups of water until the skins split and the flesh turns soft.
Mash the tamarind in its water with a fork, then press it through a strainer into a bowl. Discard the seeds and skins and keep the thick sour juice.
Add the radish and simmer until it starts to turn translucent.
Add the fish and simmer gently.
Add the mussels, cover and simmer until they open. Discard any that stay closed.
Add the okra and long beans and simmer until tender.
Stir in the tamarind juice to taste, add the chilies and season with fish sauce.
Add the shrimp and simmer until pink, then the squid until just opaque.
Turn off the heat, add the water spinach and cover until wilted. Serve right away.

tips: Mussels and shrimp are salty, so taste before adding all the fish sauce.

title: Sinigang na isda sa batuan
intro: Visayan-style fish sinigang soured with batuan and scented with lemongrass and ginger, with okra, eggplant and sweet potato leaves. Deeply sour and fragrant.

items.name: firm fish
items.note: such as maya-maya, tanigue or bangus, cleaned and cut into steaks

items.name: stalks lemongrass (tanglad)
items.note: bruised and tied in a knot

steps.text: Bring the water, onion, tomatoes, ginger, lemongrass and batuan to a boil, then simmer until the batuan are very soft.
Scoop out the batuan, mash them through a strainer back into the pot and discard the seeds and skins.
Add the fish, lower the heat and simmer gently without stirring until just cooked.
Add the okra and eggplant and simmer until tender.
Remove the lemongrass. Add the chilies and season with fish sauce.
Turn off the heat, add the sweet potato leaves and cover until wilted. Serve hot.

tips: Frozen batuan works the same as fresh. If you can only find dried batuan, use 5 or 6 pieces and simmer them a little longer.

title: Kadyos, baboy at langka (KBL)
intro: An Ilonggo sour soup of pigeon peas, pork hock and unripe jackfruit, soured with batuan. The peas turn the broth dark and earthy, and the jackfruit soaks up the sourness.

items.name: stalks lemongrass (tanglad)
items.note: bruised and tied in a knot

steps.text: Put the pork, drained pigeon peas and water in a large pot and bring to a boil. Skim off the foam.
Add the onion, garlic and lemongrass. Cover and simmer over low heat until the pork and peas are tender.
Add the batuan and simmer until soft.
Scoop out the batuan, mash them through a strainer back into the pot and discard the seeds and skins.
Add the jackfruit and simmer until tender.
Remove the lemongrass. Add the chilies and season with fish sauce and salt.
Serve hot with rice.

tips: Soak the dried kadyos overnight or they will take much longer to soften. Oil your knife and hands before cutting fresh jackfruit, since the sap is very sticky.

title: Sinanglao
intro: An Ilocano soup of beef tripe, intestines, meat and liver in a broth soured with kamias and sharpened with a little beef bile. Sour, gingery and slightly bitter.

steps.text: Put the tripe and intestines in a pot, cover with water and boil for 10 minutes. Drain and rinse to clean them.
Return the tripe and intestines to the pot with the brisket, 3 liters of water and the sliced ginger. Simmer, covered, until everything is tender.
Lift out the meats, cut them into thin strips and keep the broth.
Heat the oil in a clean pot and saute the garlic, onions and ginger strips until fragrant.
Add the sliced meats and fish sauce and stir for a few minutes.
Pour in the reserved broth, add the kamias and simmer until the kamias break down.
Add the liver and simmer just until cooked.
Stir in the bile a little at a time, tasting, until it is as bitter as you like. Season with pepper and more fish sauce.
Serve hot, topped with green onions.

tips: Beef bile is sold in small packs at markets that sell beef innards. Start with a teaspoon: a little goes a long way.

title: Sinigang na hipon sa miso
intro: Shrimp in a cloudy broth of sauteed miso and tomatoes, soured with tamarind and finished with mustard greens. Salty-sweet shrimp in a rich, sour soup.

steps.text: First, boil the tamarind in the 2 cups of water until the skins split and the flesh turns soft.
Mash the tamarind in its water with a fork, then press it through a strainer into a bowl. Discard the seeds and skins and keep the thick sour juice.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Saute the garlic, onion and ginger until fragrant, then the tomatoes until they break down.
Add the miso and stir for a minute until it smells toasty.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil and add the radish. Simmer until it starts to turn translucent.
Add the eggplant and long beans and simmer until tender.
Stir in the tamarind juice to taste, add the chilies and season with fish sauce.
Add the shrimp and mustard greens and simmer just until the shrimp turn pink.
Serve right away.

tips: For a deeper orange broth, twist the heads off a few shrimp, fry them in the oil before the garlic and press them to release their fat. Add the bodies with the rest.
